title: Pyramid Builders
tagline: Stone by stone, an immortal legacy rises from the desert.

scenes.text: Egypt, 2650 BCE. The sun hammers the desert like a bronze fist. Thousands of skilled craftsmen haul limestone blocks across the scorching sand — not as slaves, but as workers of the crown, fed and honored for their labor.

scenes.speaker: Pharaoh Djoser
scenes.text: Imhotep. I want a monument that touches the sky itself. Something the world has never seen.

scenes.speaker: Imhotep
scenes.text: Great Pharaoh, I have dreamed of it. A stairway of stone, six steps reaching to the heavens. Your name will outlast every dynasty that follows.

challenge.question: Imhotep is best described as:
options: The architect of the first pyramid
challenge.fact: Imhotep designed the Step Pyramid of Djoser around 2650 BCE — the world's first large stone structure. He was later deified as a god of medicine.

scenes.text: The truth about the pyramid builders has long been buried under legend. They were citizens of Egypt — craftsmen, physicians, engineers — who took pride in their craft and left their names carved into the stone.

challenge.instruction: Solve the ancient Egypt crossword — fill in words about Imhotep's world across and down.
challenge.fact: PHARAOH, PYRAMID, DUNE — the vocabulary of a civilisation that Imhotep helped build, raising stone mountains from the desert floor.

scenes.speaker: Imhotep
scenes.text: See how the outer casing catches the sun? White Tura limestone, polished to a mirror's sheen. From the desert, it will blaze like a second sun. That is how the gods will find us.

challenge.instruction: Navigate the treacherous passages deep inside the Great Pyramid
challenge.fact: The Step Pyramid of Djoser has six tiers and a subterranean maze of corridors. Imhotep designed every one.

scenes.speaker: Master Builder
scenes.text: Apprentice! Pharaoh demands a new pyramid: 500 paces long, 500 paces wide, 500 paces tall. Each brick is one pace by one pace by two paces. You must calculate the number of bricks before sunset — or face his wrath.

challenge.instruction: Slide the golden capstone block to the marked position at the base.
challenge.fact: The pyramids were built with a workforce of skilled, paid laborers — not slaves — who received food, medical care, and honored burial near the site.

scenes.text: Deep in the sacred chambers, the air is still and ancient. Three levels of corridors wind into darkness — each guarded by the sacred geometry of Imhotep himself. Descend through all three chambers to reach the pharaoh's eternal resting place...

challenge.instruction: Mix the royal Egyptian blue that adorned the tombs of pharaohs — the world's first synthetic pigment, made from copper, sand, and limestone.
challenge.fact: Egyptian blue (cuprorivaite) was manufactured from around 3200 BCE by heating quartz, copper minerals, and limestone to 900°C. It was traded across the ancient world and when exposed to infrared light it glows so brightly it can be detected from orbit.
